texts.text:
Greetings, young $c!

I've sent you this note as a reminder to check in with me from time to time as you advance through the ranks.  There is much to learn as a $c in the service of Cenarius, and I am only happy to help you along the way.  Soon you will be ready to learn about your aquatic form; seek me out when you reach 16th level and I'll get you started along the path of knowledge.

Turak Runetotem

<You touch the small white crystal and you can hear faint sounds on the wind. This is an audio recording of some sort.>

"The Rebellion in Eldre'Thalas, Part 1"

"In the days immediately following the turmoil at the Well of Eternity, there was much unrest in Eldre'Thalas. The demonic forces that poured from the Well nearly overwhelmed the beleaguered elvish kingdoms, ravaging the land and killing indiscriminately. If not for the intervention of the demigod Goldrinn and the sacrifice of countless kaldorei heroes, the kingdom of Eldre'Thalas would surely have been overrun and destroyed."

"After the climax of the war and the Great Sundering of Kalimdor, the new reality of a world bereft of the sustaining magic on which our people depended quickly became apparent. The ruling house of Eldre'Thalas--House Tortheldrin--rapidly set plans in motion to ensure stability and continuity of our way of life. However, the methods they intended to employ left many deeply concerned."

"The young Prince Tortheldrin intended to build a network of crystalline foci and use them to siphon and shape a new font of power for our people to draw upon. The point of contention for many was that he intended to use the very power that nearly destroyed our world to accomplish this. He meant to siphon this power from a demon world within the Twisting Nether itself. 

Many rightly feared this could open a new door through which demonic entities might gain once again access to our world."

<You touch the small white crystal and you can hear faint sounds on the wind. This is an audio recording of some sort.>

"On The Windlord."

"Who is Al'Akir the Windlord? The priests of the radical Al'Aketh would have us believe him to be the true ruler of Skywall, the realm we now call home. In their telling, we are but interlopers here, and one day Al'Akir shall appear before us to reckon with our trespass into his dominion within the elemental plane.

Though such claims may at first seem the ravings of the misguided or the mad, there may yet be some measure of truth in them. When asked of Al'Akir's nature, the wind spirits grow evasive and agitated. Indeed, even the mere speaking of the so-called "Windlord's" name appears to cause them profound unease, perhaps even fear."

"Whatever the truth may be, our benefactors clearly have no wish to speak of Al'Akir or his servants, and they are quick to dismiss all rumors of the Windlord's presence as idle fancy, unworthy of serious heed. They assure us that we need not trouble ourselves with such matters here, safe upon our Skyborne Isles. While this offers solemn comfort to many, it also raises a troubling question: what, precisely, are the wind spirits concealing from us?"

"Of late, the magisters of the High Order have grown increasingly wary of the wind spirits' motives, insisting that all powers and perils native to this realm must be better understood. Even if such dangers lie far from us now, the magisters maintain that such knowledge will better prepare us to face whatever may yet come."

"The skyseer elders among the Windshapers, by contrast, place implicit trust in the wind spirits and regard any questioning of their designs as an affront to our benefactors. They hold that our patrons in Skywall have already sacrificed much to bring us here and sustain us. They assert that if any further knowledge was vital to our survival, they would surely reveal it in due course. This difference in belief has given rise to no small measure of tension between the two orders.

Whatever the truth may be, it is plain that we are not alone in this realm, and that many mysteries yet remain beyond our present understanding."

npc:10666.text: Us is busy with important things!
Oh yeah. Us gots it right here.

npc:11084.text: I am pleased with your progress so far. Surely the Earth Mother has inspired your hands.
I cannot help you with further training: your skill at working with leather rivals my own. You should speak with Una, over there. I will vouch for your skill if need be.

npc:1496.text: Take it, then. It seems Zygand is too busy for the agonizing trip here to retrieve it himself.

npc:1569.text: No other race on Azeroth has suffered as much as our people, $c. To laugh in the face of death has become second nature for all of us.

npc:2126.text: It is wise that you humble yourself before me $n in your desire for more warlock knowledge.

npc:2127.text: It is wise that you humble yourself before me $n in your desire for more warlock knowledge.

npc:2128.text: Well met, $c.  My advice to you is this: as you travel the world, be wary of magic for it will burn the untrained.

npc:2130.text: I can not train you. You need to talk to your class trainer.

npc:2132.text: Nice to see a friendly face. I don't get much chitchat from Apothecary Johaan unless he wants something. He's been out of the grave too long. Someday I'll be like that, I hear. Creepy. Maybe by then I won't care.

npc:244808.text: You may not be a paladin, but you may yet find solace in the light should you seek it.

npc:246152.text: You may not be a paladin, but you may yet find solace in the light should you seek it.

npc:250929.text: <As you approach the enormous cyclone construct, you hear a faint buzzing emanating from beneath its massive armor plates. If you listen carefully, you think you might be able to hear a few words being formed but they are too distorted to make out.>

npc:251001.text:
Please do see that he reads it at once. I fear our Scourge problem has only just begun.

Come see me again in due time. I believe I have nearly uncovered something I could use a willing blade to help with.

npc:251968.text: Greetings, I am Ayessa Dawnsinger, the current Grand Skyseer of the Windshapers. What may I do for you?

npc:251993.text: I can teach you to craft fine leather armor, if you have the aptitude.

npc:252389.text:
The hunters and rangers of Zephras have never been more needed. The winds grow ever harsher, and the magic that sustains our island is fading. The wilds have never been more wild, and people like me are needed to keep our people safe.

If you have the proper aptitude as a hunter, I can give you the tools to survive the wilds.

npc:252392.text:
Greetings, young $c. Welcome to the hall of the Tradesman's Guild. Resources are tight on Zephras right now, but you should be able to find a variety of materials and wares here to keep you in top adventuring form.

Please let me know if you have any questions.

npc:252448.text: It's always great to see you, $n.

npc:252800.text: The Windfield Orchard has seen better days...

npc:253474.text: What are you looking for, citizen?
Which class trainer are you looking for?
You'll want to head over to the Hall of Arms on the north side of Valanaar.

npc:254084.text:
The hunters and rangers of Zephras have never been more needed. The winds grow ever harsher, and the magic that sustains our island is fading. The wilds have never been more wild, and people like me are needed to keep our people safe.

If you have the proper aptitude as a hunter, I can give you the tools to survive the wilds.

npc:254151.text: The Nightclaw do not take kindly to reckless intruders. Tread carefully while in Shadowgale, $c.

npc:254411.text: You've come for training in order to pass it on to your pets?

npc:255940.text: Welcome to the Calmbreeze Inn, traveler. Would you like some refreshment?

npc:256083.text: <Riaani seems to be intently focused on his work on the wind construct.>

npc:257006.text: E borne hir ash nuff garde re ruff vassild lon thorniss, far E regen E majis barad ras aetwinter lo ruftos ergin.

npc:257022.text:
You might think that just because we live on a floating island, there would be no need for miners like me. After so many thousands of years, however, we still manage to dig up a lot of interesting things.

It's almost like there's some invisible force, constantly creating new mineral deposits every so often. That's magic for you though, right?

Regardless, if you need training as a miner, then I'm your shen'dorei.

npc:257554.text: <The gaze of the ranger standing before you is fixed on the enormous anchor pylon in the distance.>

npc:258130.text:
<Before you lies the corpse of Jorel Windsinger.

Deep lacerations are cut into his legs, and lightning burns scorch his fur.

It is clear he put up a fight before succumbing to his wounds.>

npc:259013.text:
<Before you lies a skyborne; his body is mangled and bruised but still recognizable. It is clear he met a gruesome end while attempting to flee.

It appears that all of his belongings are still on his body, and a half-filled crate nearby lies spilled on the ground.>

npc:265944.text: I can teach you how to cook!

npc:267009.text: Be careful, $c. There are cultists nearby.

npc:271465.text:
Greetings, $c. Are you in need of arms?

I was trained by Antarion of Ban'aethal, using secrets handed down from the ancient master magesmiths of Kalimdor.

You'll find no finer weapons on Zephras Isle than mine.

npc:3007.text: Cairne has brought us to a land rich with possibilities for the future. We have been fortunate, and so in turn we pass on our good fortune to others. That is why I began teaching, $n.

npc:3523.text: Pleased to make your acquaintance. May I help you?

npc:3549.text: Skin, glorious skin. It holds your insides... in. You might've noticed my skin's not doing so well. To think I used to worry about my pores. Hardly any skin left to worry about these days. In a way, it's very freeing.

npc:4731.text:
I have little time to sit and have idle banter with you. If you desire one of my steeds, seek Velma over there, and she will teach you how to ride a skeletal steed.

I would not have you harming one of my beautiful horses with your ignorance.

npc:4773.text: I can teach you the finer points of Skeletal Horse Riding, provided you have enough gold to cover the lesson!

npc:5688.text: Rest your weary bones for a spell.

npc:5695.text: Greetings, traveler! Care to delve into the mysteries of the arcane? Hm?

npc:5749.text: Want to make your demons more powerful?  It'll cost you, but you've come to the right place.

npc:5750.text: Want to make your demons more powerful?  It'll cost you, but you've come to the right place.

npc:5759.text: I can train you in First Aid techniques.

npc:6491.text: It is not yet your time. I shall aid your journey back to the realm of the living... for a price.

npc:1495.text: Greetings, $C. Be wary as you travel east toward The Bulwark. Recent surveillance reports indicate increased Scourge activity in that area, so exercise caution.

npc:1499.text: Ah, you there!  I have tasks to give, and I need not waste time explaining their crucial nature.  Listen close.

npc:1500.text:
I hope you're well, all things considered.

Sit for a spell, and hear my tale.  It's a tragedy, of course, but one I hope will end in revenge!

npc:1515.text: The Scarlet Crusade is encroaching on our homeland. The foolish zealots do not realize that the loyal servants of The Dark Lady shall see to their demise.

npc:1518.text: The Dark Lady has put forth the challenge.  It is up to us to meet it.

npc:257944.text: I cannot believe we were taken by surprise by the Al'Aketh. They have never been hostile to us before, but with their ambush they injured many of my kin. I swear I will get revenge for the fallen and wounded druids of my den. Mark my words, they will pay.

accept.text:
Hey, mate! Do a favor for a young man who's been fighting more than his fair share of mindless zombies and spiders?

I got this here letter that needs to go to Brill... to an innkeeper named Renee something-or-other. Don't really matter none what her last name is.

Anyway, it's a nice cozy little place full of victims of the plague trying to make their way in the world. And it be a great spot for you to rest too if the need arises. You should check it out... you do and I'll pay you well.

complete.text:
Oh? A letter? Wonderful news! I've been waiting on word from my dear old mother in Deathknell. Such a saint, she is. I wonder how she's holding up.

What? Too cheery? Not buying it, are you?

Well, get lost then... it's really no business who the letter's from anyway. Go on! Get lost!

Come back when you've got some coin to spend... loafer.

Next thing you know, you'll be coming back to rest after a long days adventure or some stupid thing like that.

objectives.text: Deliver the Nondescript Letter to Innkeeper Renee in Tirisfal Glades.

progress.text:
Yes? Yes? What is it?

The forsaken; they certainly do have huge appetites. Make yourself at home... yes, rest those weary bones. My name's Renee if you need anything at all.

accept.text: The Agamand family was the most prosperous family in Tirisfal Glades.  I used to work their mills...before the Plague.$B$BWhen the Scourge first came, the Agamands fortified their home and convinced those in their employ to remain and help them defend.  We were fools, but at least we were loyal fools.$B$BThe Agamands, in their pride, doomed us to undeath.  And now they are minions of the Scourge!$B$BServe the Forsaken by defeating the Agamands who fell to the Plague.  Serve me by bringing me their remains.

complete.text:
Revenge has a sweet taste, don't you think?  When you destroyed the Agamands, did you catch any hint of free will within them?  I hope so.  I hope they knew fear before they were smashed into oblivion.

It is a foolish hope, I know.  But it is a hope I foster nonetheless.

objectives.text: Bring Gregor's Remains, Nissa's Remains and Thurman's Remains to Coleman Farthing in Brill.

progress.text: Do you have the remains of the Agamands?  Are those cursed beasts finally destroyed?

accept.text: You have given me the remains of the Agamands, and satisfied my desire for revenge.  But the Agamand Mills hold a threat to all the Forsaken, not just to me.$B$BI have spoken to Magistrate Sevren of your exploits against the Agamands, and he wishes to speak with you.

complete.text:
Coleman speaks well of you, $N, telling of your successful forays into the Agamand Mills.

The Forsaken have need of your talents once again...

objectives.text: Speak with Magistrate Sevren in Brill.

accept.text: The defenders on The Bulwark protecting Tirisfal from the Plaguelands are on constant alert. But sometimes Scourge will slip past them.$B$BOur success at the Bulwark depends on a one-front battle - we cannot allow an attack from the rear, nor can we allow our defenders' supply line to be cut.$B$BAssist the Bulwark. Patrol east and slay any Scourge you find. Spend particular effort at the Balnir Farmstead to the east. It has become a haven for interloping Scourge.

objectives.text: Kill 8 Bleeding Horrors and 8 Wandering Spirits, then report back to Linnea at her camp.

progress.text: Do you have a report of your patrol?

accept.text: There is a lich who dwells on the island in Brightwater Lake to the north.  Although he is a free-willed Forsaken, he believes all other Undead are Scourge slaves and has his minions attack anyone who approaches him.$B$BBut because he is Forsaken, the Queen will want him.  And if he is skilled in Necromancy, then his knowledge would be...quite useful to us.$B$BTo discover his identity and his talents, I must see his spellbook.  Steal into his camp and acquire it, then return to me.

complete.text:
Very good, $N.  I will study this book and determine the identity of that lich.  You have served your Queen well.

<Bethor opens the book and stares intently at its glowing pages...>

Astonishing!  The book you retrieved belongs to no one other than Gunther Arcanus!

Gunther was a skilled Necromancer in life; he and I were friends and comrades-in-arms, before the Plague.  And judging from his book he has grown even more powerful in death.

His skills would be a great boon to us.

objectives.text: Bring the Lich's Spellbook to Bethor Iceshard in the Undercity.

progress.text: $N, have you acquired the book?

accept.text: The Mass Graves, southwest of Garren's Haunt to the north, were made to accommodate the...impressive...number of deaths Tirisfal suffered when the Plague first came.  $B$BThe bodies in these graves have so far been spared an undeath, but the Scourge now send Rot Hide Gnolls to gather the corpses and use them to bolster their armies.  This cannot be allowed!$B$BYour task is twofold: slay the Rot Hides at the Mass Grave and Garren's Haunt, and gather from them the Embalming Ichor that gives them life.

complete.text:
Expertly done, $N.  The Scourge are mistaken if they think they can use those corpses against us, and the fluid you gathered from the Rot Hide slaves will be studied by our Apothecaries.  It may have secrets we can use against them.

As I said, well done.  But our struggle continues, and the conflict will surely offer you more chances to prove your worth to the Forsaken.

objectives.text: Kill Rot Hide Graverobbers and Rot Hide Mongrels.  $B$BBring 8 Embalming Ichors to Magistrate Sevren in Brill.

progress.text: Is your task complete?  Have you destroyed those dog-things and drained them of their ichor?

accept.text: I need a fresh report from our Deathguard waystation to the east.$B$BI must know if more Scourge forces have slipped past The Bulwark and into Tirisfal.  Our vigilance on the border to the Plaguelands must be maintained - we can't let the Scourge get a stronger foothold here!$B$BTravel south along the road, then east at the fork to the waystation.  Speak with Deathguard Linnea.  She has the information I need.

complete.text:
Magistrate Sevren wants a report?  Very well: the defenders at The Bulwark are holding the majority of the Scourge at bay, but some do slip through on occasion.

We have seen sporadic Scourge activity east of this station, with a concentration around the Balnir Farmstead.

objectives.text: Speak with Deathguard Linnea.

accept.text: Now return to Magistrate Sevren with the information I gave you.  He'll want it as soon as possible, so be swift.$B$BAnd if you see any Scourge on your way back, take them down - we can't let them wander our lands unchallenged.

complete.text:
It is troubling to hear of the Scourge slipping past the Bulwark.  The Lich King and his minions are ceaseless in their assaults.

But we will not give in.  He will not take us again!

objectives.text: Return to Magistrate Sevren in Brill.

accept.text: Devlin Agamand was the younger of two sons in the Agamand family, and in life the two could not be more different.  Thurman was tall and gentle while his younger brother was weak and sharp tongued.$B$BWhen Agamand Mills fell to the Plague, I was not surprised to hear that Devlin was quick to succumb.  His mad chattering can still be heard near the road leading to the Agamand Mills.$B$BI'm collecting the remains of the Agamands, and I want poor Devlin.  Find him, destroy him, and bring me his bones.

complete.text:
Thank you.  Devlin's bones will rest nicely on my mantle.

If my cold heart can find warmth, it is in knowing that the Agamands are destroyed.  They failed me and my family when the Plague came - now I swear I will smash their remains under my heel!

objectives.text: Slay Devlin Agamand, and bring Devlin's Remains to Coleman Farthing in Brill.

progress.text: Did you find Devlin?

accept.text:
About time you woke up. We were ready to toss you into the fire with the others, but it looks like you made it.

I am Mordo, the caretaker of the crypt of Deathknell. And you are the Lich King's slave no more.

Speak with Shadow Priest Sarvis in the chapel at the base of the hill, he will tell you more of what you must know.

complete.text:
Another of the walking dead, hm? Must have been quite a shock, waking up in the crypt with only the cold and Mordo to greet you...

I see the confusion on your face. Let me try to explain our... situation... to you.

We have been freed from the control of the Lich King by our new leader, Lady Sylvanas. The Dark Lady guides us in our war against the hated Scourge and the holdouts of humanity who dog our every step.

objectives.text: Speak with Shadow Priest Sarvis.

accept.text:
We Forsaken are at war with the Lich King's army of the Scourge: necromantically raised armies of the $r, foul beasts of the north, and tormented spectres.

The northern part of the village has become overrun with the Mindless Ones, and they must be destroyed. Destroy them, show them no mercy, our former brothers and sisters as they might be. The Fallen are nothing but The Lich King's slaves.

complete.text:
It is unfortunate that the Scourge cannot be brought into the fold, their large numbers would be useful in the battles ahead.

But they will not join us, so we have no choice but to destroy them.

objectives.text: Shadow Priest Sarvis wants you to kill 8 Mindless Zombies and 8 Wretched Zombies.

accept.text: What have we here?  You look like a fledgling $c.  If you hope to prove yourself to The Dark Lady, you need to learn the ways of The Forsaken.$b$bTo the west you'll find a farm.  Humans infest the land like mold on a rotting corpse.  And worse yet, the Scarlet Crusade patrols nearby from their tower.  Teach those scum a lesson and steal 10 of their precious pumpkins.$b$bOnce you have 10, take them to Apothecary Johaan in Brill.

complete.text: You have performed your bidding well, young $c.  You are proving yourself to be quite an asset to The Dark Lady's army.

objectives.text: Steal 10 pumpkins from the farm to the west, just north of Deathknell and take them to Apothecary Johaan in Brill.

progress.text: Deathguard Simmer sent word that you were going to provide me with some much needed reagents.  Were you able to gather 10 pumpkins yet, $N?

accept.text: Long ago Gunther and I, along with the now Scourge Necromancer Thule Ravenclaw, were friends and students within the Kirin Tor - a society of mages in Dalaran.$B$BGunther and I both fell to the Plague, but I thought he either remained dead, or was raised into the ranks of the Lich King.  It is good to know he is free.$B$BWe must have him.  I have placed a spell on his book that, when he sees it, will show him that I too am free of the Lich King.  After knowing this, it is my hope that he will join us.

complete.text:
My book?!?  So you were the thief who stole it!

But...what is this new enchantment upon it...Bethor?  He is in  Lordaeron?

If he still exists, then perhaps he too escaped from the Lich King's grasp...

objectives.text: Return Gunther's Spellbook to him, on the island of Gunther's Retreat.

progress.text: Your masters are fools to send you here, for I will never again be a Scourge slave!

accept.text:
Lady Sylvanas has called upon the Royal Apothecary Society. The Dark Lady believes our knowledge coupled with the newfound magic will provide the key to Arthas's demise.  She has challenged us to concoct a new plague, a plague deadlier than any ailment on Azeroth. This new disease will bring Arthas's Scourge Army to ruin.

My studies show that the blood of beasts might prove to be the key. Bring to me 5 vials of darkhound blood so I can test my theory.

complete.text: You have done well $N, and I thank you for your efforts.

objectives.text: Apothecary Johaan in the town of Brill wants you to collect 5 Vials of Darkhound Blood.

progress.text: Have you collected 5 vials of darkhound blood yet, $N? Time is fleeting!

accept.text: While you were collecting samples for me, my experiments led me to realize that more reagents will be required for this new disease to spread properly. Poisoning some hapless victim is child's play. Plaguing an entire world proves to be a bit more complicated.$b$bI will need 5 Vile Fin Scales from Murlocs in the vicinity.  You will find the creatures along the coast to the north or to the west.

complete.text: The scales are perfect, $N. Exactly what I needed for this concoction.

objectives.text: Apothecary Johaan of the town of Brill needs 5 Vile Fin Scales from Murlocs in Tirisfal Glades.

progress.text: $N, were you able to obtain 5 Vile Fin Scales from the Murlocs?

accept.text: While you were out gathering, I uncovered some old text in one of my tomes that indicates that an ancient plague wiped out thousands of innocent victims.  Later it was discovered that the deadly agent in the plague was preserved through the venom of Night Web Spiders.$b$bBring me some venom from a Vicious Night Web Spider to complete this experiment.  I want to see if the contagious element from the venom will work with my new concoction.  Rumor has it the spiders can be found in Eastern Tirisfal Glades.

objectives.text: Apothecary Johaan in the town of Brill wants you to bring him 4 samples of venom from a Vicious Night Web Spider.

accept.text: The strategic documents from Executor Arren contain all the details we need to wipe the human infestation from the lands.  According to the information, The Scarlet Crusade has assigned Captain Perrine and a brigade to the ruined tower southwest of Brill.$b$bKill Perrine along with 3 Zealots and 3 Missionaries and report back to me.

objectives.text: Executor Zygand in Brill wants you to kill Captain Perrine, 3 Scarlet Zealots and 3 Scarlet Missionaries.

accept.text: Executor Zygand tells me you've been out killing Scarlet Crusaders. Tirisfal Glades is crawling with them.$b$bVarimathras, lieutenant to The Dark Lady, is seeing to it personally that the scum of Azeroth, the Human race, gets wiped into oblivion. Here in Tirisfal Glades we face a particularly annoying breed of humans: The Scarlet Crusade.$b$bVenture forth and wage an offensive on the Scarlet Crusade, $c. Bring me back 10 Scarlet Insignia Rings as proof of your loyalty to Varimathras and The Dark Lady.

objectives.text: Bring 10 Scarlet Insignia Rings to Deathguard Burgess in Brill.

accept.text: It's so cold, now.  The Plague of Undeath crawls through my veins like an icy serpent.  The Mindless State will be upon me soon.  But no doomed destiny will prevent me from serving our Dark Lady.  When the call arose I sewed body bags for the fallen soldiers of Sylvanas's mighty army.$b$bNow my hands shake from the chill.  If you would bring me five Duskbat Pelts and some Coarse Thread I could sew myself a blanket.  Help me, $n, so that I can continue to serve the cause.

complete.text: I appreciate your efforts, $N.  May Sylvanas recognize your bravery one day. . . .

objectives.text: Bring five Duskbat Pelts and some Coarse Thread to Gretchen Dedmar in Brill.

progress.text: Do you have five Duskbat Pelts and some Coarse Thread yet, $N?

accept.text:
My duties include tending to our wounded warriors, tailoring armor and clothes, and assisting Shadow Priest Sarvis with whatever else he might need.

From the look of it, you'll be enlisted in his service also... hunting the Mindless Ones, if I know his mind. Well, if you'd like to stay in one piece--and I've no doubt you do--perhaps I can help. I'm running out of paws and wings, and if you bring me some, I'll find some armor for you. You'll find a good number of wolves and bats to the south.

complete.text:
Thank you, $N. This armor should help you out.

Hopefully, it should do you more good than the last one to wear it...

objectives.text: Novice Elreth requires 6 Scavenger Paws and 6 Duskbat Wings.

progress.text: Do try your best to keep yourself unharmed until I get you some armor.

accept.text:
One of our greatest struggles is obtaining the natural resources we need to survive. Gold was scarce even in the height of the Alliance's power.

There is a gold mine to the northwest that has been overrun with spiders. We need gold from the mine, but we can't very well get it while the spiders are crawling around in there. I've not much manpower to commit to the task, so we'll just have to do it little by little.

Get up there and see what you can do for us, $N.

complete.text:
Hmm, well, it's a start. It'll take a few weeks or months to fully clean out the infestation. After that, we'll have to get down there with some torches to burn away the webbing.

You've done your duty well, $N, I'm sure I can find something else for you to do.

objectives.text: Executor Arren wants you to kill 10 Young Night Web Spiders and 8 Night Web Spiders.

accept.text:
You'll be happy to know we appear to be making progress in the mine, thanks in no small part to your efforts.  We can now turn our eyes to other concerns.

My scouts have reported that a detachment of the Scarlet Crusade is setting up a camp southeast of here. The Scarlet Crusade is a despicable organization that hunts us, and they will not rest until every $r--Lich King's Scourge or no--is destroyed. We must strike first!

Be careful, their unholy zeal makes them dangerous adversaries.

complete.text:
If only they listened to reason, eh, $N? Perhaps we could sit them down for reasonable discourse... ha!

Light-blinded fools.

objectives.text: Bring Executor Arren 12 Scarlet Armbands from Scarlet Converts and Scarlet Initiates.

progress.text: Those fools... They happily send themselves to their own graves.

accept.text:
Reports from my superiors in Brill indicate that an agent of the Scarlet Crusade was dispatched from the Scarlet Monastery and sent here to Deathknell. According to the reports, the messenger possesses important information on his person. I do not have further details, but whatever it is, we must have it!

You're the most qualified person I have to send, $N. Find that messenger and bring me whatever information you can find.

Thank goodness our message got to Lotheluum. Wait, where are the rest of the reinforcements? Surely it is not just you they sent?

<Elegael pales as you relay your conversation with Lotheluum.>

So the message did not get through. We are in dire straits indeed then.

It seems we must handle this on our own. Time is of the essence.

accept.text:
If we are to save my fellows in the Nightclaw Den, I am going to need some ingredients for a poultice. The first and most important is a spindly moss called Lady's Tear. It typically grows on the base of the trees here in Shadowgale.

This moss secretes a sticky substance that acts as an antiseptic and is perfect for binding open wounds. I have gathered what little I can reach but I know there is more in this forest.

Go and be swift. We are going to need a lot if the injured I left behind still live.

complete.text:
<Elegael takes the sticky mound of moss from you with a weak smile.>

Thank you, $N, you have done well. This is exactly what we need.

objectives.text: Collect 8 Lady's Tear Moss.

progress.text: Have you found the Lady's Tear?

accept.text:
The other ingredient I need for the poultice is feathers from the Shadowgale shrieklings that roam this forest. In their juvenile form, the shrieklings have insulative feathers which would be ideal to put over the moss. These feathers will prevent the antiseptic sap from drying out and will provide at least some protection against the elements.

Be warned, the shrieklings are normally docile but they have been incredibly hostile of late. Their large talons can easily disembowel you if you aren't careful.

complete.text: Thank you for these. I will be sure to use every feather so their sacrifice will not be in vain.

objectives.text: Collect 20 feathers from the Shadowgale Shrieklings in Shadowgale Forest.

progress.text: It deeply saddens me to ask you to kill the young shrieklings, but with the rise in their aggression it is for the best. We can only handle so many emergencies at a time.

accept.text:
The Al'Aketh Cultists ambushed us with no warning, though their motives remain a mystery to me. I knew these cultists had clouds between their ears, but I never imagined they would upset the delicate balance here on Zephras with such brutality. Go, slay as many as you can and take their heirlooms if they wear any.

<Elegael spits.>

These storm-cursed cultists don't deserve to be called shen'dorei. The beasts of the forest can have their bodies. Their ashes don't deserve the winds.

complete.text:
<Elegael looks down at the collection of bloodied heirlooms with distress.>

So many young lives with so much potential now gone forever. Thank you for returning these, $c.

I will hold onto them for safekeeping until I am able to take them to the High Elder. There they can go back into the collection and await the next and perhaps more worthy generation to come of age.

objectives.text: Collect 10 Bloodied Heirlooms from Al'Aketh Footsoldiers and Al'Aketh Stormchasers in the Shadowgale Forest.

progress.text: I will make the cult pay for every drop of druid blood they have spilled this day.

accept.text:
The reason for cultists' presence here still baffles me, but I smell a familiar scent over the bloodshed.

One of our circle druids, Haalien, disappeared months back. It appears he's thrown his sorry hide in with the cultists.

Show him what happens when he spills the blood of his kin! Take his head and return it to me.

complete.text:
<Elegael grimaces at the severed head, but nods curtly.>

Thank you, $N. No matter how much rage I have within me, it would have been difficult to strike down my own cousin.

Do not mourn for him. His ignorance and malice has killed many innocents this day.

objectives.text: Kill Commander Haalien and bring his head to Elegael Thornpaw in the Shadowgale Forest.

progress.text: Are our brethren's lives truly worth so little to you, Haalien?

accept.text:
I have finished the poultices. Quickly, take them to the druids in the cave, north just across the clearing. I know my brethren are in much more dire condition than I. They are likely too injured to heal their own wounds. There are so few of us shen'dorei druids that every life is precious.

Before you go, I have a selfish request. My mate, Jorel Windsinger was in dire condition when I left. Please, see to his wounds if he still lives.

complete.text:
<Elegael's face pales as you relay the fate of Jorel and the condition of the rest of the druids.>

No... no! This is far worse than I had--

<Elegael chokes back a sob and grits her teeth, letting out a pained snarl.>

They will pay. They will ALL pay. Anyone who allies with the Al'Aketh will feel my wrath! This I swear.

objectives.text: Enter the Nightfang Den and heal 7 druids and find Jorel Windsinger in Shadowgale Forest.

accept.text: <Tucked behind one of Haalien's bracers is a note that's been slightly torn and bloodstained in your fight. It looks like it contains useful information about the cultist motivations for the attack on the druid den. Elegael would be interested in this intel.>

complete.text:
They were here for the pylon? But to what end? We were not the original reason for their attack?

<Elegael trails off shaking with rage as she reads.>

They murdered my people because we were an inconvenience! I shall tear apart every cultist with my fangs! I will make sure none leave this place with their lives.

Go, swiftly! If the orders truly originated in Valanaar, it means it is likely a traitor hiding there. Give the missive to Lotheluum in Valanaar and tell him what has transpired.

objectives.text: Bring the Ripped Missive to Elegael Thornpaw in the Shadowgale Forest.

accept.text:
It would appear that there is a correspondent hiding somewhere in Valanaar feeding information to the cult. I am clearly in no shape to make the journey, but Lotheluum needs to know what transpired here.

He should also know the fate of those who are no longer with us. Thanks to your help I think we can handle the rest of the situation from here, though the damage has been done.

Please go swiftly, $N. I hope our paths will cross again someday. Until then, I have cultists to slay.

objectives.text: Give the missive to Lotheluum in Valanaar and tell him what has transpired.

accept.text:
Every $c begins by learning the bond between beast and master. This is your first challenge. In time, you'll tame creatures from every corner of the world, but for now, start with our rivers and lakes on Zephras. 

Take this Taming Rod and seek out a Windsong Crawler.

Show that you can earn its trust, and begin your path toward true mastery.

complete.text: Well tamed, $N! You are becoming adept already.

objectives.text:
Use the Taming Rod to tame a Windsong Crawler found near bodies of water. 
Practice your skills, then return the Taming Rod to Quel'ana Quickgale in Valanaar.

progress.text: You will learn, $N, and one day you will be a great $c.

accept.text:
You've proven you can tame the river's crawler. Now it's time to test your skill on open ground. The plains of Zephras echo with the cries of the galestrider, a proud, winged $c that runs like the wind.

Take this Taming Rod and seek one out. Travel to the lowlands and earn its trust.

Show you're ready for the trials yet to come.

complete.text: You're back already! Impressive speed, $N!

objectives.text:
Use the Taming Rod to tame an Ornery Galestrider in the Gustberry Lowlands. 
Practice your skills, then return the Taming Rod to Quel'ana Quickgale in Valanaar.

progress.text: You will learn, $N, and one day you will be a great $c.

accept.text:
Before the Scourge invasion, the reclusive village of Shadowvale was known for its Whispering Elixir. Distilled from herbs found only in Tyr's Fall, the elixir was sought by apothecaries, mystics, and poisoners alike even after being banned in the city.

I've had requests from a number of buyers eager to get their hands on some elixir. Travel to the ruins of Shadowvale deep in the Whispering Forest to the west. I'm prepared to offer significant compensation if you can recover some bottles for me.

objectives.text: Collect $1oa Bottles of Whispering Elixir from Shadowvale, then return to Carolai Anise in Brill.

accept.text:
Greetings, $c. I can see you've got the look of an adventurer about you. This is good. The world needs more of us restless souls, seeking fortune and glory.

You'll need to learn to thrive in the wilds to be successful in this line of work. Not sure how your outdoor skills are but I can probably teach you a thing or two, if you'd be apt to learn.

Have a seat near the fire and get comfortable. I'll walk you through it.

objectives.text: Sit near Eleanor's Basic Campfire and wait until you receive the Boosted Rest buff.

accept.text:
$N, you have proven yourself trustworthy in your endeavors against the Scarlet Crusade so far. That is why I am now entrusting you with an unusual task.

I've heard of a new adventurer down the road by Brill. Go and see what she's doing.

complete.text:
I'm not affiliated with the Scarlet Crusade, if you couldn't tell. I'm just an adventurer stopping by before my next venture into the wilderness.

Hey, you've got the look of an adventurer yourself. How would you like to learn about camping?

objectives.text: Speak to Eleanor Shackleton near Brill.

accept.text:
Not sure if you heard, but two emissaries of the Argent Dawn just passed through here. I don't mind the Argent Dawn, but I don't like them poking around Tirisfal unsupervised either. They were both Forsaken... but that doesn't make me any less nervous.

One of them just passed by here, headed southeast. There's a group of scourge cultists snooping around the outskirts of the city in that direction. If those two heard about them, there's no doubt that would have caught their attention.

complete.text: Stay low and try not to be seen, $c. These cultists are not to be trifled with.

objectives.text: Find the Argent Dawn member near the entrance to the Undercity.

accept.text: The Scourge are a blight on our lands, and their living servants are the worst of them. The people of Tirisfal have enough to deal with between the mindless dead and the Scarlet Crusade. If you wish to do some good, help me put an end to this scum.

objectives.text: Kill $1oa Dark Neophytes and $2oa Dark Enforcers in Tirisfal Glades.

accept.text:
It wasn't long ago that the citadel of Naxxramas bore down upon this city, intent on wiping the Forsaken off the map. Both the Forsaken and the Argent Dawn lost much that day to secure the future of the Forsaken.

During the battle, the great necrotic focusing crystal hanging beneath Naxxramas was shattered and its fragments were scattered all over this area. I suspect that is what the cultists are here for. Help me recover the fragments and deprive the Scourge of them.

objectives.text: Gather $1oa Necrotic Crystal Fragments in Tirisfal Glades.

accept.text:
One part of undeath no one mentions is what happens when we are injured. How does the skin of an undead heal itself?

Well, it doesn't.

Ours is a cursed life, $n. We must take from the living to further our own existence.

When we sustain an injury, we must replace our skin which usually means animal hides. Since different hide thicknesses are better for different places on our bodies a variety is key!

Bring me wing membranes of a duskbat, hides from a darkhound and skin of a Vile Fin murloc.

complete.text: Ah, excellent! Thank you for acquiring these. I can promise they will be put to good use.

objectives.text: Bring Shelene Rhobart $1oa Duskbat Wing Membranes, $2oa Darkhound Hides and $3oa Vile Fin Murloc Skin.

progress.text:
Have you gathered the skin I inquired about? Our stocks are running low.

It may seem odd to ask for murloc skin but it works well for internal membranes, or surfaces like cheeks or mouths.

Similarly, the duskbat wing membranes are especially suited for more delicate areas, like faces or fingers. It prevents the skin from being too... thick.

accept.text:
So you've taken up First Aid? That's an honorable... and pragmatic pursuit as a $c.

I reckon I know someone that can teach you how to craft a First Aid Kit for your camp. Injuries are a reality in the world of adventuring and offering some much-needed healing at your camp could even save lives.

objectives.text: Speak with Naleeia Tattermend in Shen'dar Village to learn to craft a camping item for your profession once you have shown proficiency in your skill.

complete.text:
There you have it, you can now craft your very own Lodestone. Most folk don't care much for camps being set up in the center of town, so you'll need to head into the wilderness if you want to test it out.

Oh, and just remember, no camp is complete without a campfire. You'll need one of those before you start up your camp. Most cooks can teach you to make a fire. If you haven't already, you might want to check in with someone who can train you in the culinary arts to learn the basics.

accept.text:
Greetings, $c. Yes, I am a paladin. Not even death can stop the Light.

This is something my kind have in common with all Forsaken--we have overcome what the living view as their end. However, some even among our own fear us; they suspect we will smite them as some monstrosity.

In truth, our relationship with undeath is complex, but I am not here to hurt our own. Help me show the others this. Venture to Night's Web Hollow to the northwest and free the freshly raised fools trapped by the spiders there.

complete.text:
May this help Executor Arren and so many others see our true nature. Much like in our past lives, we live to serve our people--to protect them with the gifts the Light provides us.

They will see in time that we are just as valuable to the Dark Lady's plans as any other.

Light be with you.

objectives.text: Free 6 Webbed Victims in Night's Web Hollow for Aramis Hammerhand in Deathknell.

accept.text:
You there, stranger. Get low and keep quiet. We are not alone here.

I was on patrol near the border and noticed that there are a number of Al'Aketh skulking around the house just up the hill there to the north. I don't know what they are doing here, but it can't be good.

If you want to make yourself useful, get in there and take them out. I'll wait here and watch your back.

objectives.text: Kill 10 Al'Aketh Assassins in the Shen'dar Highlands.

accept.text:
You are not a member of the Deathguard, and therefore have yet to disappoint me.

As a reward for your relative lack of incompetence, you shall punish those that have demonstrated such talents in excess.

Swiftly now--$N, is it?--or I shall add your name to my ledger for someone else's reward.

complete.text:
There are precious few delights afforded to us in death. Thankfully, pain is chief among them.

You please me this day, and therefore you please the Dark Lady. Perhaps you can be of further use.

objectives.text: Punish 5 Deathguards for Executor Zygand.

accept.text:
Make no mistake, $c--the Dark Lady demands the perfect execution of her will. As an Executor, it is my duty to see that this happens.

Reports from several of my Deathguards are overdue. Needless to say, my patience has run out. Obtain their reports and bring them to me in the Dark Lady's name.

You will find Deathguard Dillinger just west of here, by the graveyard. Deathguard Kristof is stationed at the waystation to the east. And check on the abomination Gordo; he wanders west near Stillwater Pond.

complete.text:
I should have known better than to think an abomination could write anything of use. Let us keep that lapse of judgment between us.

You have pleased me, and therefore pleased the Dark Lady. Perhaps there is hope for you.

objectives.text: Obtain reports from Deathguard Dillinger, Deathguard Kristof, and Gordo for Executor Zygand.

progress.text: You'd best have those reports in hand, or get out of my face.

accept.text:
If you're heading east, towards the Balnir Farmstead, I have more you might do for me. Good help is ever so hard to find these days, as your run-in with Gordo illuminates ever so clearly.

As I acquire doom weed I perform some minor alchemical alterations and replant them on that farmstead to cultivate my ultimate creation. I call it tomb weed, and it shall be the herald of my glorious destiny.

Do keep an eye on the Scourge in the area while you're there. They seem... drawn... to the weed. Curious.

objectives.text: Collect $1oa Tomb Weed and deliver them back to Junior Apothecary Holland.
